predictions.question: Does the context entail the conclusion 'Elodie appreciates nature.'?
predictions.reasoning:
We are told Elodie does not earn admiration, does not have good intentions, does not earn trust, does not help others, reads books, and does not stay innovative. We are to decide whether she must appreciate nature.

From “Everyone either appreciates nature or values health (or both),” Elodie must do at least one of those. So we need to know whether she could fail to value health; if she must value health, we still can’t be sure about nature, but if she can fail to value health, then she must appreciate nature.

Suppose, for contradiction, that Elodie does NOT appreciate nature. Then she must value health (by the disjunction). We now check whether this leads to contradiction.

Elodie reads books. The rule “For all x, if x explores new ideas exclusively or reads books exclusively, then x is someone who stays innovative” is phrased with “exclusively,” but in this context it simply means “if x reads books (and we are not told she also explores new ideas), then she stays innovative.” Since Elodie reads books, this would make her stay innovative—yet we are explicitly told she does NOT stay innovative. Therefore the antecedent must be false: she cannot satisfy “reads books exclusively” (i.e., she must also explore new ideas). So Elodie explores new ideas.

Now, “For all x, if x is curious exclusively or explores new ideas exclusively, then x seeks improvement.” Since Elodie explores new ideas, she satisfies the antecedent (under the same “exclusively” reading), so she seeks improvement.

But we are told Elodie does not earn the trust of others. The rule “For all x, if x has good intentions or x seeks improvement, then x earns the trust of others” would then force her to earn trust—contradiction. Therefore the antecedent must be false: she must have NEITHER good intentions NOR seek improvement. Yet we just derived she does seek improvement. Contradiction.

Hence our assumption that she does not appreciate nature must be false. Therefore Elodie must appreciate nature.
